Well, let me think about this year. I'm 60, been working these fields for 40 years, so I mostly do what I've always done. No sense changing much when it's worked.

I've got 7.5 mu total. Most of it — about 5 mu — is cotton, that's my money crop. The other 2.5 mu I keep for wheat and then maize after, so we've got our own flour and some grain. Can't buy everything, prices go up every year.

It's just me and the old lady at home now. Kids are in the city. So labor is tight — I can do the planting and spraying myself with the sprayer on my back, but cotton picking in autumn, we're slow. Sometimes I ask relatives to come help, or my neighbor's family and we trade days.

**On the cotton (about 5 mu):**
I'll plant end of April when the soil warms up, same as always. I use the seed I buy from the shop in town — the agent recommends one every year, I just buy what's cheap, 30-some yuan a mu. Before planting I spread what we call the "big fertilizer" — one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, that's about 50 jin, and then when the cotton starts setting bolls I put down maybe half a bag of urea per mu. That's how everyone around here does it. If I put too much the cotton grows too tall and the bolls don't set right, my father taught me that.

Cotton needs spraying — bollworm is bad some years. I spray 3, 4 times usually. Watered from the well twice, once after planting if it's dry, once when it's flowering. Water costs money — electricity for the pump — so I don't water more than I have to.

Last year I got maybe 230 jin of lint per mu. Price was okay. I'm hoping for similar this year.

**On the wheat (2.5 mu, already in the ground since last October):**
Put down one bag of compound fertilizer at planting. Right now the wheat is getting tall, I need to go topdress urea soon — half a bag per mu — and water it. Then another watering when it's filling. If I see the bugs, I spray, but usually just one herbicide in spring for the weeds. Harvest beginning of June, hopefully get 400 jin per mu like usually.

**On the maize (2.5 mu, after wheat, plant in mid-June):**
As soon as the wheat combine goes through, I have to hurry — week at most. Son-in-law brings the little planter, we put the maize right into the stubble. I buy hybrid seed, everyone buys hybrid, can't save it yourself. One bag compound at planting, one topdress of urea when it's knee-high. Water once, maybe twice if no rain. Spray once for weeds early. Harvest end of September so I have time to turn the land over for wheat again.

Money's tight. I got maybe 2000-some yuan saved for inputs. Can't afford to experiment. What works, works.
